outputs.L3:
The invention relates to a display processing method and apparatus for an electronic device having a display that includes a plurality of display areas. More particularly, the invention concerns an electronic device in which a display is divided into a first display area having a substantially flat shape and a second display area extending from the first display area and having at least a partially curved shape, and to a technique for processing image or display data for the respective display areas.

The electronic device may include a housing, a display provided on or in the housing, a first processor, a second processor, and at least one memory operatively connected to one or both of the first processor and the second processor. The housing may define an external appearance of the electronic device and may support the display such that different portions of the display are exposed through or arranged on different regions of the housing.

The display may include a first display area and a second display area. The first display area may be exposed on one surface of the housing and may be formed as a substantially flat area. The second display area may extend from at least one edge or side of the first display area and may be formed to be at least partially curved. For example, the second display area may be bent or curved along a side surface of the housing, thereby allowing information to be displayed not only on the front surface of the electronic device but also on a curved or side region of the device.

The at least one memory may store instructions which, when executed, cause the first processor to process data to be displayed on the first display area. The first processor may generate or render display data corresponding to the flat first display area and may provide the processed data, or information associated with the processed data, to the second processor.

The at least one memory may also store instructions which, when executed, cause the second processor to process data received from the first processor. Based on the data provided by the first processor, the second processor may generate display data suitable for the second display area. In particular, the second processor may perform processing adapted to the shape, size, resolution, curvature, orientation, or display characteristics of the curved second display area, so that content can be appropriately displayed on the second display area.

Accordingly, the electronic device may separately or cooperatively process display data for the flat first display area and the curved second display area by using the first processor and the second processor. This configuration may improve display processing efficiency and enable content to be displayed properly across both the flat and curved portions of the display.
outputs.L4:
An electronic device may include a display having multiple display regions with different physical shapes. In one example, the display includes a first display area that is substantially flat and a second display area that is curved, bent, or otherwise non-planar. The first display area may correspond to a main viewing region of the device, while the second display area may extend along an edge, side, or peripheral portion of the device.

To efficiently process image data for these different regions, the electronic device may use a dual-processor display processing structure. A first processor may be configured to process image data associated with the flat first display area. This may include receiving image content, performing scaling, color correction, frame composition, or other display-related processing for the first area, and generating display data suitable for output to that portion of the display.

The first processor may then provide at least part of the processed data, control information, timing information, or related display parameters to a second processor. The second processor may be configured to generate display data for the curved second display area. Because the second area has a curved geometry, the second processor may perform additional processing, such as coordinate mapping, image correction, distortion compensation, brightness adjustment, or edge-region rendering, so that content displayed on the curved area appears properly aligned and visually consistent.

By dividing the display processing tasks between the first processor and the second processor, the device can render content across both the flat and curved display areas in a coordinated manner. This arrangement allows the flat region and the curved region to operate together as part of a single display system, while still enabling specialized processing for the different shapes and viewing characteristics of each region. As a result, the electronic device can provide a continuous or integrated visual experience across display areas having different geometries.

counterfactuals.prompt: Write a patent-style abstract for an electronic device with a display having a flat main area and a curved edge area, where a first processor handles content for the flat area and a second processor generates content for the curved area.
counterfactuals.output: An electronic device is disclosed. The electronic device includes a display having a substantially flat main display area and a curved edge display area extending from at least one side of the main display area. A first processor is configured to generate, render, or control first image data corresponding to content displayed in the main display area. A second processor, distinct from the first processor, is configured to generate, render, or control second image data corresponding to content displayed in the curved edge display area. The display presents the first image data on the main display area and the second image data on the curved edge display area, thereby enabling independent or coordinated control of content output on the flat and curved portions of the display.

counterfactuals.prompt: Draft a “various embodiments of the present invention” description for a display processing method and apparatus involving a housing, a divided display, two processors, and memory storing instructions for processing first-area and second-area display data.
counterfactuals.output:
Various embodiments of the present invention provide a display processing method and apparatus capable of processing display data for a display that is divided into a plurality of display areas.

In one embodiment, an electronic apparatus includes a housing, a display supported by or disposed in the housing, a first processor, a second processor, and a memory operatively coupled to at least one of the first processor and the second processor. The display may include a first display area and a second display area divided from the first display area. The memory may store instructions that, when executed, cause the electronic apparatus to obtain first display data corresponding to the first display area and second display data corresponding to the second display area, process the first display data by using the first processor, process the second display data by using the second processor, and output the processed first display data and the processed second display data to the display so that an image is displayed across the first display area and the second display area.

In another embodiment, the first processor may be configured to perform image rendering, image correction, scaling, color conversion, frame-rate conversion, or timing control with respect to the first display data, and the second processor may be configured to perform image rendering, image correction, scaling, color conversion, frame-rate conversion, or timing control with respect to the second display data. The first processor and the second processor may process the first display data and the second display data independently, in parallel, sequentially, or in coordination with each other.

In still another embodiment, the memory may store instructions that cause the electronic apparatus to divide source image data into the first display data and the second display data based on a boundary between the first display area and the second display area. The boundary may be a physical boundary, a logical boundary, a fold line, a seam, a bezel region, a hinge region, or a virtual division line defined by display-driving circuitry or software. The instructions may further cause the electronic apparatus to synchronize the processed first display data and the processed second display data such that visual discontinuity at or near the boundary is reduced.

In yet another embodiment, the display may be a flexible display, a foldable display, a rollable display, a tiled display, a multi-panel display, or a single display panel logically divided into a plurality of areas. The first display area and the second display area may have the same size or different sizes, and may be arranged side-by-side, vertically stacked, diagonally arranged, or arranged in any other suitable configuration.

According to various embodiments, a display processing method includes obtaining, by an electronic apparatus including a housing and a display divided into a first display area and a second display area, first display data corresponding to the first display area and second display data corresponding to the second display area; processing the first display data by a first processor; processing the second display data by a second processor; and displaying, on the display, an image based on the processed first display data and the processed second display data. The method may further include dividing source image data into the first display data and the second display data, synchronizing output timing of the first processor and the second processor, correcting image characteristics of at least one of the first display data or the second display data, and outputting the corrected display data to corresponding display areas.

In some embodiments, the first processor may be disposed in a first portion of the housing corresponding to the first display area, and the second processor may be disposed in a second portion of the housing corresponding to the second display area. Alternatively, the first processor and the second processor may be disposed in a common portion of the housing and may communicate with display-driving circuitry through separate or shared data paths.

In some embodiments, the memory may store instructions that cause the apparatus to determine whether the display is in an unfolded state, folded state, expanded state, contracted state, portrait state, landscape state, or multi-window state, and to process the first display data and the second display data based on the determined state. For example, when the display is in a folded state, the apparatus may activate one of the first display area or the second display area and deactivate or reduce power to the other. When the display is in an unfolded state, the apparatus may process the first display data and the second display data to form a continuous image across the first display area and the second display area.

In various embodiments, the apparatus may further include display driver circuitry configured to receive the processed first display data and the processed second display data and drive pixels of the first display area and the second display area. The display driver circuitry may include a first display driver corresponding to the first display area and a second display driver corresponding to the second display area. The first processor may provide the processed first display data to the first display driver, and the second processor may provide the processed second display data to the second display driver.

In various embodiments, the memory may store instructions that cause at least one of the first processor or the second processor to perform compensation processing based on luminance, color, gamma, refresh rate, resolution, pixel density, temperature, aging information, or calibration information associated with the first display area or the second display area. The compensation processing may reduce differences in display characteristics between the first display area and the second display area.

In various embodiments, the first processor may be a main processor, an application processor, a graphics processing unit, a display processing unit, an image signal processor, a timing controller, or a display driver integrated circuit, and the second processor may be another main processor, application processor, graphics processing unit, display processing unit, image signal processor, timing controller, or display driver integrated circuit. The first processor and the second processor may be implemented as separate chips, separate cores in a single chip, separate functional blocks in a system-on-chip, or any combination thereof.

According to various embodiments, distributing processing of first-area display data and second-area display data between the first processor and the second processor may reduce processing load, increase display refresh performance, reduce latency, reduce power consumption, improve image quality, or support larger or higher-resolution divided displays.

counterfactuals.output: An electronic device includes a display having a first display area that is substantially flat and a second display area that is curved. The electronic device further includes a memory storing instructions and a plurality of processors configured to execute the instructions. A first processor processes first display data corresponding to the first display area, and a second processor processes second display data corresponding to the second display area independently from the processing of the first display data. The processed first display data and the processed second display data are provided to the display to render an image across the first display area and the second display area.
